steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9-inch square baking dish.

Whisk flour, 1/2 cup sugar, and baking powder together in a mixing bowl. Stir in milk and melted margarine until a batter forms; scrape into the prepared baking dish. Scatter blackberries over top, then sprinkle on remaining 1/2 cup sugar. Pour in water.
Bake in the preheated oven until batter rises and top is brown, 45 minutes to 1 hour. Cool 1 hour before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Best in Show Blackberry Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: This prize-winning blackberry cobbler, starring fresh blackberries plus the usual supporting cast – sugar, flour, and milk – is the perfect summer dessert.
raw_recipe.name: Best in Show Blackberry Cobbler

review.reviewBody: This is BY FAR my favorite cobbler recipe. I tripled the recipe but I added 4 Cups of Blackberried, 2 Cups of Raspberries and 1 Cup of Blueberries. The colors difference in the berries made it very pretty. Great when it's warm with Vanilla ice cream...

I really enjoyed this. I used Frozen Blueberries. I cut the water back to 3/4 cup since I used frozen. Added the juice of about a third of a medium Lemon and could have used more. I mixed water lemon juice and sugar in the measuring cup with the blueberries and stirred it up. poured that mixture over the batter. It is a loose batter and this cooked up nicely. I would add more berries next time.

I made this again with strawberries & apricots. I used 1/2 c. wheat flour & 1/2 c. white flour. Instead of just milk in the batter, I subbed 1/2 the amount with buttermilk. I also use butter, not margarine. I added a teaspoon of vanilla to the milk mixture before I poured it into the batter. Only other change--used a 1/2 c of brown sugar, instead of white to sprinkle over the berries before baking. Overall, it was much more flavorful. The recipe is very easy & can be used with pretty much any fruit, if you know what flavorings to add.

I also use butter, not margarine. I added a teaspoon of vanilla to the milk mixture before I poured it into the batter. The recipe is very easy & can be used with pretty much any fruit, if you know what flavorings to add.

I have made this recipe many times. The first time was with fresh blackberries. That turned out delicious, so when I had a bumper peach harvest this year I started using this recipe with peaches and continue to do so with my fresh frozen peaches. The only thing I do differently is that I use much less sugar in the final step. I just sprinkle sugar on top and it turns out to only be almost 2 tablespoons. I can't imagine what it would be like to dump a 1/2 cup of sugar on it at the end. And I use butter instead of margarine.

It is so easy and turns out great every time. Thank you!!

Great and easy. When doing with peaches, change final 1/2 cup sugar to 1/4 cup white/1/4 cup Brown. Blend and sprinkle over fruit. Then sprinkle cinnamon and a little nutmeg before adding water. Fabulous peach cobbler recipe.

This is so simple/easy and not just for blackberries, this is great for peaches, strawberries and bluberries or any combination of just about any fruit you can think of. I made 2 changes to the recipe. I reduced the sugar to 1/4 cup white sugar & 1/4 cut brown sugar. You don't need another 1/2 cup of sugar to pour on top, my fruit was sweet enough and the extra sugar isn't necessary. I just sprinkle a couple of tablespoons overtop right when it comes out of the oven. The other change I made was to add 1 teaspoon of baking powder to make it a total of 3 - really makes it fluffy! Pouring the water over the top just before baking seems crazy but trust the process, it comes out perfect.

This is very similar to my peach cobbler recipe handed down to me which I make with blackberries, or any other fruit. I have a few differences : 1 1/2 C water instead of 1 C, 1/4 cinnamon added to the sugar sprinkled over the fruit, and I always add 1 t almond extract to the milk. I cream butter and sugar, then alternate adding milk and flour/baking soda/1/4 t salt mixture. It is my absolute favorite!! With the extra water, I get a juicy sauce; delicious!!

Delicious! I used fresh dewberries and added 1/2 tsp. of cinnamon. Used butter instead of margarine. Combining the suggestion of another reviewer with this recipe, I mixed the butter, 1/2 c. sugar, water, and berries in a pan and brought to a boil. I mixed 1/4 c. sugar with the batter and sprinkled 1/4 cup sugar over the top.

I read other reviews , so I used this recipe as a guide and adjusted to my taste. For the crust I added sour canned milk and salt. For the mix I added 3 cups of blackberries, 1 cup of sugar, salt, cinnamon, molasses (I wanted brown sugar but I forgot), lemon juice, vanilla extract, I cooked the mix till hot and bubbly and spooned crust on top 8x8 pan baked 45 min at 350. Perfect.

I made this for a social gathering and it was LOVED by all our guests. The batter on the bottom with blackberries and water on top (what the heck?) feaked me out, but I went for it! It turned out beautiful. Berries sunk in perfectly and there was a nice golden brown topping after about 50 min. I made a 1.5 batch and used a 9 by 11.5 pan. I also added a splash of vanilla and dash of cinnamon to the batter. This will be my go to recipe for blackberry cobler!
My first time making it so I did the exact amount of ingredients. Very good!!
Made as written, took a deep breath and poured the one cup of water on top. Can't explain it, but it's a 5 star. Ice cream optional.

I canned blackberry cobbler filling this summer. I followed this recipe for the dough and poured my filling on top. It came out amazing! I have blueberry pie filling and apple pie filling to try next.
I tried 4 different cobbler recipes this summer and this one was by far the best. Pouring water on top seemed so bizarre but it turned out to be perfect and so easy.
Quick and easy cobbler, and turned out absolutely beautiful. A great use for seasonal berries.

This was really good. It seemed like a ton of sugar so I left out about a tablespoon but I think I should have just put it in because it wasn't too sweet. I did sprinkle about 1/4 cup of sugar over the blackberries and let them sit in a bowl for about 10 mins. I think that helped to sweeten them. Then I put them on top of the batter and sprinkled the remaining sugar on top. This was good but tasted better the 2nd day. I was searching for a good cobbler recipe. I don't think I'll look any further.

This was a very easy recipe to put together. Quick and simple. Rating 4 stars because for me at least, it was a bit too sweet. This even in the face of the fact that the blackberries that I had were pretty tart. I may cut the sugar a little bit next time. But we did enjoy it, with fresh whipped cream. Maybe the sweetness led us to consume smaller portions! I'd try it again for sure.
Neither me or my husband cared for it. I"t was too cake-ish. The batter didnt have much flavor. Wont be making again
